CausalChain: NAFLD -> upregulation of FTO -> aberrant m6A demethylation on metabolic/inflammatory mRNAs -> increased mRNA stability and translation -> enhanced lipogenesis and chronic liver inflammation -> formation of a pro-tumorigenic microenvironment -> HCC development
Hypothesis: In NAFLD-associated liver carcinogenesis, increased FTO-mediated m6A demethylation in hepatocytes dysregulates key metabolic and inflammatory gene expression, thereby promoting a microenvironment that facilitates the initiation and progression of hepatocellular carcinoma.
Abstract: Recent studies have highlighted the role of m6A RNA modifications in liver carcinogenesis, particularly through the modulation of mRNA stability and translation by various m6A regulatory proteins. Building upon these insights, we propose that in the context of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), aberrant upregulation of m6A 'eraser' proteins, notably FTO, drives dysregulated m6A demethylation on mRNAs encoding key metabolic and inflammatory regulators. This altered epitranscriptomic landscape results in enhanced mRNA stability and translation of genes that promote lipogenesis and chronic inflammatory signaling, thereby fostering a pro-tumorigenic microenvironment. In this model, the cumulative effect of metabolic reprogramming and inflammation accelerates the transition from NAFLD to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This hypothesis not only integrates m6A-mediated RNA regulation into the pathogenesis of liver cancer but also suggests potential therapeutic targets in the m6A regulatory machinery for early intervention.
